purpose: The hosts a link may resolve to. scripts/gates-compliance.mjs reads this as Gate 3 and the judge page template reads it to mark which of a biography's sources are secondary. One file, so the gate and the page can never disagree about what is primary.

primary.law.shu.edu: Seton Hall's own faculty directory, for the fact that a judge teaches there. An institution's roster of its own appointments is the record of it, the same ground the Courthouse News PDFs were admitted on. Directory pages only: the domain also serves panel and speaker bios, which are accounts.

secondary.opinions: None. A link to an opinion or a filing must resolve to a primary host. The gate errors otherwise.
secondary.biographies: Permitted, and marked as secondary on the page. No primary source carries a magistrate judge's biography: FJC covers Article III judges, the court's own judge pages are chambers and procedures, and a judicial-milestones page gives an appointment date. Where the court published a Notice to the Bar announcing the appointment, that is primary and comes first; for appointments before roughly 2023 there is none.
secondary.requirement: A secondary biography source must carry a source_label saying what it is, because the label is what the reader sees. The gate errors on an unlabeled one.
secondary.disclosure: policy.json carries the disclaimer the magistrate pages render.
